items.question: What is my educational background?
items.answer:
Rudra holds a Master of Computer Science from the University of Wollongong, Australia, completed between 2023 and 2025 with a major in Machine Learning and Big Data [[cite:2,8]]. This degree was awarded in August 2025, carried 96 credit points, and was supported by the UOW Postgraduate Academic Excellence Scholarship, a 30% tuition fee waiver [[cite:8]]. He graduated with High Distinctions in Programming and Data Structures, Web Development, Strategic Network Design, and the Professional Capstone Project, along with Distinctions in Big Data Analytics, Security Essentials, AI and Cybersecurity, and System Analysis and Project Management [[cite:4]]. His coursework spanned computer vision, machine learning, big data, and security topics such as Computer Vision Algorithms and Systems, Modern Cryptography, Data Management Systems, and AI and Cybersecurity [[cite:6]].

Prior to this, Rudra completed a Bachelor of Technology in Computer Science and Engineering with a Data Science specialisation at Gujarat State Fertilizers and Chemicals University in Vadodara, India, from 2019 to 2023 [[cite:2,7]]. During this program he received the Achiever's Award for the 2021-22 academic year [[cite:7]]. His undergraduate coursework included foundational subjects like mathematics and communication skills, core computer science topics such as programming, data structures, operating systems, and computer networks, as well as electronics and hardware subjects including digital electronics and microprocessor interfacing, alongside professional courses and industrial internships [[cite:3]].

items.question: Which AI/ML frameworks have I used?

On the AI/ML side specifically, you have worked with scikit-learn and PyTorch, along with RAG and hybrid retrieval approaches combining BM25 and vector search, using ChromaDB as a vector database [[cite:1]]. You have also used LLM providers such as Groq (Llama-3.3-70B), Together AI, Anthropic Claude, and the OpenAI API [[cite:1]].

Your LinkedIn profile additionally lists TensorFlow, Hugging Face Transformers, Hugging Face Inference API, and Claude API among AI/ML tools, along with ReAct agent and multi-agent systems work [[cite:2]]. Your professional summary also highlights that you build AI systems with production engineering practices including hybrid retrieval, evaluation harnesses, and guardrails [[cite:3]].

items.question: What is the title of the patent?
items.answer: The patent is titled "Intelligent Face Recognition System Using Deep Recurrent Neural Network" [[cite:1,3]], filed as Indian Patent Application No. 202211058943 A [[cite:3,5]].

items.question: What is the patent application number?
items.answer: The patent application number is 202211058943 A, filed on 15 October 2022 for the Intelligent Face Recognition System Using Deep Recurrent Neural Network [[cite:2,3,4]].

items.question: What neural network architectures does the patent describe?
items.answer: The patent describes an intelligent face recognition system that combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a recurrent neural network (RNN) [[cite:5]]. In this design, the CNN and RNN work together within a key generation module to produce a consistent key value from sample facial images of a person [[cite:5]]. The overall system is titled as using a deep recurrent neural network approach for face recognition [[cite:3]].

items.question: What is the patent journal number?
items.answer: The patent was published in Patent Office Journal No. 42/2022, dated 21 October 2022 [[cite:1,3]].

items.question: What is the Cognitive-Chair project about?
items.answer:
The Cognitive-Chair is an AI-based brain-sensing wheelchair designed to assist paraplegic and quadriplegic individuals [[cite:5]]. It uses a brain-sensing headband employing electro-oculography to capture neural signals, which are transmitted to a mobile application and then to the wheelchair so it can be operated according to the user's neuro signals rather than physical input [[cite:4]]. The project was developed to address limitations of both manual and powered wheelchairs, such as reliance on physical strength, difficulty navigating obstacles, high costs, and maintenance needs [[cite:8]].

This research was carried out during a B.Tech degree and won the Best Paper Award at the 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Speech Technology (AIST-2022), organised by the Centre of Excellence - Artificial Intelligence [[cite:1]][[cite:7]]. It was later published on IEEE Xplore, and the work also contributed to an Indian government patent filing for an Intelligent Face Recognition System [[cite:5]][[cite:6]]. Rudra Joshi is listed as a co-author on this publication, alongside Kshitij Joshi, Abhilasha Vyas, Smit Joshi and others [[cite:5]][[cite:7]].

items.question: What are the main brainwave frequencies mentioned?
items.answer: The main brainwave frequencies mentioned in Electroencephalography are Gamma, Beta, Alpha, Theta, and Delta [[cite:1,2]]. Gamma waves are linked to the acquisition of new information in the brain [[cite:2]]. Beta waves are associated with focused attention on cognitive and real-world tasks [[cite:1]]. Alpha waves are connected to calm, pleasant thinking and represent the brain's default resting state [[cite:1]]. Theta waves are most common during sleep and deep meditation [[cite:1]]. Delta waves have low frequency and are associated with deep tranquillity, relaxation, and dream formation [[cite:1]].

items.question: What microcontroller is used in the wheelchair design?
items.answer: The Cognitive Chair design uses an Arduino microcontroller to process data received from the Android application and translate it into control signals for the wheelchair motors and other hardware [[cite:1]]. The system architecture also describes a microcontroller linked to the mobile application, which executes the control algorithm before directing the wheelchair's movement [[cite:2]].

items.question: Which bluetooth module does the system use?
items.answer: The system uses the HC-06 bluetooth module for wireless transmission of signals between the headband and the microcontroller [[cite:2]].

items.question: What is a Brain-Computer Interface according to the paper?
items.answer:
A Brain-Computer Interface (BCI), also called a Brain-Machine Interface or Direct Neural Interface, is a technology that lets users communicate with machines or external devices using brain signals instead of the brain's normal output pathways of peripheral nerves and muscles, giving humans the ability to control machines directly and effortlessly [[cite:1]]. It is considered one of the most promising and increasingly popular technologies for assisting and enhancing communication and control for people with motor paralysis caused by conditions such as paraplegia, quadriplegia, stroke, spinal cord injury, cerebral palsy, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis [[cite:2,7]].

A BCI system is composed of three main parts: electrodes that record electric, magnetic, or metabolic brain activity; a processing pipeline that interprets these signals, extracts relevant features, decodes patterns, and outputs commands; and a computer or external device that acts on those generated commands [[cite:5]]. BCIs are further classified into invasive, non-invasive, and semi-invasive types, depending on how sensors are placed relative to the brain [[cite:5]].
